  GUIDELINES:
    - "Overall energy: moderate deficit ~300-500 kcal/day below estimated maintenance to support fat loss while minimising hypoglycaemia risk."
    - "Protein: 1.2-1.6 g/kg/day general; increase to 1.2-1.8 g/kg/day during Phase 3 to support recovery with higher intensity."
    - "Carbohydrates: distribute evenly across meals (3-4 meals/day); prefer low glycaemic index carbs, fibre and combine carbs with protein and fat to blunt postprandial spikes."
    - "Peri-workout: on heavy Phase 3 sessions add ~10-20 g carbs pre/post session; post-session aim 20-40 g carbs + 20-30 g protein within 1-2 hours."
    - "Fasted cardio: check pre-exercise capillary glucose. If <5 mmol/L (or per clinician guidance) consume a small fast-acting carbohydrate snack before activity. Carry glucose tablets/juice during early sessions."

  GUIDELINES:
    - "Intermittent fasting (IF) can be used by some people with type 2 diabetes but requires careful monitoring and clinician/dietitian coordination; do not start IF without discussing with prescribing clinician."
    - "Risk considerations: fasting increases hypoglycaemia risk, particularly around exercise and if on multiple glucose-lowering medications. Although metformin alone has lower hypoglycaemia risk, individual variability exists."
    - "If proceeding: start with conservative protocols (e.g., 12:12 or 14:10 time-restricted eating) rather than aggressive windows (16:8 or longer) and trial for short periods while monitoring glucose."
    - "Meal timing and training: avoid long fasts on days with high-intensity or long-duration training. Schedule resistance sessions after a meal when possible, or include a small pre-workout snack before early-morning training."
    - "Fasted cardio: if continuing fasted morning cardio while using IF, ensure pre-exercise capillary glucose is checked; if <5 mmol/L consume a small carbohydrate snack before exercising."
    - "Nutrition quality: during eating window maintain the programme nutrition guidelines — protein 1.2-1.6 g/kg/day, even carbohydrate distribution across meals, emphasis on low-GI carbs, fibre and healthy fats."
    - "Cheat meals: incorporate weekly planned cheat meal within the eating window; avoid using cheat meals to break long fasts unpredictably."
    - "Hydration and electrolytes: maintain fluids during fasting periods (water, sparkling water, unsweetened tea). If fasting >16 hours consider electrolyte intake (sodium, potassium) if symptomatic and per clinician advice."
    - "Monitoring: check capillary glucose frequently during initial 2-4 weeks of IF (pre-meal, pre/post exercise, bedtime) to detect hypoglycaemia or large glucose variability. Record readings, symptoms and food timing."
    - "Adjustments: reduce fasting duration or stop IF if experiencing recurrent hypoglycaemia, dizziness, excessive fatigue, or poor training performance. Consider shifting to less aggressive time-restricted windows."
    - "Weight loss and glycaemic control: IF may produce modest weight loss for some but is not inherently superior to continuous energy restriction; priority should be sustainable eating patterns, medication safety, and stable glucose control."
    - "Medication coordination: if new glucose-lowering drugs are started or doses change, re-evaluate IF with prescriber before continuing."
    - "Referral: strongly recommend dietitian and diabetes clinician involvement before initiating IF to individualise plan and monitoring."
    - "Pregnancy and other contraindications: IF is not recommended in pregnancy, eating disorders, or other clinical conditions — consult clinician."

VISITATION
  RECOMMENDATIONS:
    - "Trial structure: begin with 12:12 for 1-2 weeks, progress to 14:10 if tolerated, and only consider 16:8 after clinician sign-off and demonstrated stable glucose readings."
    - "Exercise scheduling: prefer resistance training within eating window or with a small pre-workout snack; reserve higher-intensity sessions for fed state during adaptation."
    - "Logging: keep a 2-week diary of fasting window, meals, exercise and glucose readings for clinician review."
    - "Stop criteria: recurrent glucose <4 mmol/L, syncopal episodes, symptomatic hypoglycaemia, or clinician advice."
    - "If approved to continue IF: maintain weekly cheat meal within eating window and follow the existing nutrition and training plan's monitoring guidance."

NUTRITION
  GUIDELINES:
    - "Energy target: moderate deficit ~300-500 kcal/day below estimated maintenance to support fat loss while minimizing hypoglycaemia risk during higher intensity Phase 3."
    - "Protein: 1.2-1.8 g/kg bodyweight per day in Phase 3 to support recovery with increased intensity."
    - "Carbohydrate distribution: spread evenly across meals (3-4 meals/day); increase peri-workout carbohydrate slightly in Phase 3 (add ~10-20 g carbs pre/post heavy sessions) to support performance and glycaemic stability."
    - "Fast-cardio and IF considerations: check pre-exercise capillary glucose; if <5 mmol/L consume small carbohydrate before activity. Post-session consume 20-40 g carbs with 20-30 g protein."
    - "Cheat meal structure: allow one planned cheat meal per week (single meal, not a day); place after training when possible to use improved insulin sensitivity. Monitor BG before and 1-2 hours after initial cheat meals."
    - "Fat: 25-35% of total calories, emphasis on mono- and polyunsaturated fats (olive oil, nuts, fatty fish)."

NUTRITION
  GUIDELINES:
    - "Overall energy: moderate deficit ~300-500 kcal/day below estimated maintenance to support fat loss while minimising hypoglycaemia risk."
    - "Protein: 1.2-1.6 g/kg/day general; increase to 1.2-1.8 g/kg/day during Phase 3 to support recovery with higher intensity."
    - "Carbohydrates: distribute evenly across meals (3-4 meals/day); prefer low glycaemic index carbs, fibre and combine carbs with protein and fat to blunt postprandial spikes."
    - "Peri-workout: on heavy Phase 3 sessions add ~10-20 g carbs pre/post session; post-session aim 20-40 g carbs + 20-30 g protein within 1-2 hours."
    - "Fasted cardio: check pre-exercise capillary glucose. If <5 mmol/L (or per clinician guidance) consume a small fast-acting carbohydrate snack before activity. Carry glucose tablets/juice during early sessions."
    - "Pre-workout small options: e.g., 150 g plain Greek yogurt + 1/2 cup berries; small banana + 20 g protein powder; 2 rice cakes + 1 tbsp peanut butter + 100 g cottage cheese."
    - "Quick post-workout snacks: 150 g Greek yogurt + small fruit; 1 scoop whey + 1 rice cake; 150 g cottage cheese + 2 rice cakes; smoothie with 1 scoop protein and 1/2 banana."
    - "Intermittent fasting (IF): may be attempted with caution. Start conservative (12:12 → 14:10) and only progress (16:8) after clinician/dietitian sign-off and stable glucose readings. Avoid long fasts on heavy training days."
    - "Cheat meals: one planned cheat meal per week (single meal, not a full day). Place after training when possible, keep portion reasonable, include some protein and fibre, monitor BG before and 1-2 hours after initial cheat meals."
    - "Hydration & electrolytes: maintain fluids; increase attention during high-intensity weeks and long sessions; consider electrolyte intake if sessions are long/sweaty."
    - "Fat: 25-35% of calories, prioritise mono- and polyunsaturated fats (olive oil, nuts, fatty fish)."
    - "Alcohol: limit intake; avoid on heavy training days; alcohol can increase hypoglycaemia risk."
    - "Weight loss pace: target ~0.25-0.5 kg/week for sustainable loss and glycaemic stability."
    - "Micronutrients: ensure adequate vitamin D, calcium and iron; refer to dietitian if concerned."
    - "Medication: continue metformin as prescribed. If other glucose-lowering meds are used or doses change, consult prescriber before IF, fasted cardio or increasing training intensity. Monitor for hypoglycaemia."
    - "Monitoring: frequent SMBG during initial weeks of changes — pre/post exercise, pre/post fasted cardio, pre/post cheat meals, and bedtime for first 1-2 weeks of Phase 3. Keep a log of glucose, food, timing and symptoms."
    - "Adjustments: if recurrent hypoglycaemia, excessive fatigue, dizziness or poor training performance occur, reduce fasting duration or training intensity, or increase carbohydrate intake and consult clinician."

VISITATION
  RECOMMENDATIONS:
    - "Progression: increase load when top of rep range is achieved for 2 consecutive sessions; use conservative 2.5-5% load increases in Phase 3 and allow extra recovery if glucose instability occurs."
    - "Fasted cardio: prioritise low-to-moderate intensity initially; increase duration gradually; always check pre-exercise glucose and carry fast-acting carbohydrate until stable."
    - "IF trial: begin 12:12 for 1-2 weeks, progress to 14:10 if tolerated; only attempt 16:8 after clinician sign-off and stable SMBG."
    - "Cheat meal guidance: plan one weekly cheat meal after training when possible; monitor glucose response initially and avoid heavy alcohol."
    - "Recovery: prioritise 7-9 hours sleep, protein-rich meals, hydration and active recovery sessions. Consider scheduled deloads as included."
    - "Referral: recommend concurrent dietitian and diabetes clinician involvement for medication timing, personalised nutrition, and SMBG targets."
    - "Safety: stop exercise and treat if hypoglycaemia symptoms occur; carry fast-acting carbohydrate during all sessions. Cease IF or reduce fasting if recurrent hypoglycaemia or adverse symptoms."
    - "Logging: keep a 2-4 week diary of food timing, SMBG, exercise and symptoms for clinician/dietitian review."
